ledger.claim_text: Jakarta is sinking at up to 10 inches (25 cm) per year in northern districts like Muara Baru, making it one of the fastest-sinking megacities on Earth.
ledger.source_title: NASA Earth Observatory / Bandung Institute of Technology (ITB) Geodesy Research
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Geodetic GPS monitoring shows northern Jakarta subsided by up to 4 meters between 1997 and 2020, with peak subsidence rates exceeding 20-25 cm (10 inches) annually.

ledger.claim_text: Excessive groundwater extraction through unregulated deep wells drains porous underground aquifers, causing the unconsolidated alluvial clay soil to compact and deflate.
ledger.source_title: Hydrogeology Journal: Groundwater extraction and land subsidence in Jakarta, Indonesia
ledger.publisher: Springer Nature / International Association of Hydrogeologists
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Because less than 40% of Jakarta had access to piped water networks, massive industrial and domestic groundwater extraction depressurized deep confined aquifers, triggering soil consolidation.

ledger.claim_text: Over 40% of northern Jakarta currently sits below sea level, protected only by concrete sea walls and dikes that face high-tide monsoon surges.
ledger.source_title: National Capital Integrated Coastal Development (NCICD) Master Plan
ledger.publisher: Indonesian Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas)
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Approximately 40% of northern Jakarta is below mean sea level, with high astronomical tides reaching up to 1.5 meters above existing ground levels.

ledger.claim_text: The Great Garuda Master Plan proposes a $40 billion, 32-kilometer (20-25 mile) outer sea wall across Jakarta Bay designed in the silhouette of the mythical Garuda bird.
ledger.source_title: NCICD Phase B Technical Framework / Witteveen+Bos & Royal HaskoningDHV Consortium
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: The outer sea dike is an estimated $40 billion megaproject with a 32 km offshore barrier creating an enclosed retention basin in Jakarta Bay.

ledger.claim_text: Offshore breakwaters utilize multi-ton interlocking concrete tetrapods and graded rock revetments to dissipate incoming wave energy during monsoons.
ledger.source_title: Coastal Engineering Manual: Design of Concrete Armor Units and Rubble Mound Breakwaters
ledger.publisher: US Army Corps of Engineers / Deltares
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Concrete armor units (tetrapods, accropodes) interlock to create porous protective outer layers that prevent erosion of the core dike material under intense wave impact.

ledger.claim_text: In 2019, Indonesia officially resolved to relocate its capital city to Nusantara, carved out of the tropical forest of East Kalimantan on Borneo island.
ledger.source_title: Indonesian Law No. 3 of 2022 on the State Capital (UU IKN) & Presidential Declaration
ledger.publisher: Government of the Republic of Indonesia / Nusantara Capital Authority
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: President Joko Widodo announced the capital relocation from Jakarta to a 256,000-hectare site in East Kalimantan due to acute flood vulnerability, traffic congestion, and ground subsidence.

ledger.claim_text: Over 40 polder systems and massive pump stations like Waduk Pluit must run constantly to discharge trapped river runoff over sea walls into the Java Sea.
ledger.source_title: Jakarta Emergency Dredging Initiative (JEDI) & World Bank Polder Assessment
ledger.publisher: The World Bank / Jakarta Provincial Government
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Because gravity flow is impossible when land is below sea level, polder retention reservoirs and high-capacity centrifugal and Archimedes pumps lift urban runoff into the sea.

ledger.claim_text: Engineering coastal megastructures vs. managed urban retreat represents a critical modern paradigm for low-lying coastal deltas worldwide.
ledger.source_title: IPCC Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (SROCC)
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Hard coastal defenses face technical limits and high capital maintenance costs, prompting urban planners to balance engineered barriers with managed inland migration.
